name: Fairmont Banff Springs
insider_take: Known as the "Castle in the Rockies," this legendary 1888 grand dame sits majestically overlooking the Bow Valley, where Scottish baronial architecture meets untamed wilderness.
whats_special: Built by the Canadian Pacific Railway as a luxury wilderness retreat, the Fairmont Banff Springs is Canada's first resort hotel and features its own championship golf course designed by Stanley Thompson. The hotel's Gothic Revival turrets and limestone façade have made it an iconic landmark visible from throughout Banff National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
pro_tip: Book a room in the original Painter Tower for authentic castle vibes, or visit the hotel's legendary Rundle Bar, where the signature cocktail "Bow Valley" was created in 1969.
dont_miss: The hotel's world-class Willow Stream Spa features mineral hot springs therapy, and the nearby Bow Falls (a 5-minute walk) offers spectacular photo opportunities. The hotel also houses Canada's largest hotel ballroom and has hosted royalty including King George VI and Queen Elizabeth.
pros: Iconic castle-like architecture in stunning Canadian Rockies setting
World-class spa and multiple dining options including award-winning restaurants
Year-round outdoor activities including golf, skiing, and hiking access
Luxurious rooms with mountain or valley views and premium amenities
cons: Premium pricing reflects luxury mountain resort positioning
Large historic property may require walking distances between facilities
